draft.emotion: a practical and common part of daily life, steady and functional
notes: In Spain, 'coche' is the standard word for a car. In most of Latin America, people say 'el carro' or 'el auto' instead.
Note the preposition in 'en coche' (by car), without an article: 'Voy al trabajo en coche'.

senses.definition: A road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries a small number of people.

examples.text: Mi padre va al trabajo en coche todos los días.
examples.translation: My father goes to work by car every day.

draftBefore.emotion: a practical and common part of daily life, steady and functional
notes: In Spain, 'coche' is the standard word for a motor car. In many Latin American countries, you will hear 'auto' or 'carro' instead.
Do not confuse this with 'vagón' or 'tren', which refer to parts of a train.

senses.definition: A road vehicle with four wheels and an engine that can carry a small number of people.

examples.text: Mi padre conduce el coche al trabajo todos los días.
examples.translation: My father drives the car to work every day.
examples.emotion: matter-of-fact and routine, describing a daily habit

senses.definition: A carriage or a section of a train used to transport passengers.

examples.text: El tren tiene seis coches para pasajeros.
examples.translation: The train has six carriages for passengers.
examples.emotion: observational and descriptive, noting a detail about a train

faults.quote: Do not confuse this with 'vagón' or 'tren', which refer to parts
faults.why: Contradicts sense 1; also 'tren' is the whole train, not a part of one.

faults.quote: A carriage or a section of a train used to transport passengers.
